report:
## Olive Oil and Stroke Risk: What the Evidence Shows

The claim has meaningful support, though it comes with important caveats.

**Strongest evidence – randomized controlled trial:** The PREDIMED trial, a landmark Spanish RCT with ~7,500 high-cardiovascular-risk participants followed nearly 5 years, found that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil reduced cardiovascular events, "particularly stroke," compared to a control lower-fat diet (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/pdf/10.1161/hypertensionaha.113.03353). This is the most rigorous type of evidence available, since it uses hard clinical endpoints rather than self-reported outcomes.

**Supporting cohort and meta-analysis data:** A dose-response meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies found that each 25g/day increment in olive oil intake was associated with a 24% reduction in stroke risk (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261954820_Olive_oil_consumption_and_risk_of_CHD_andor_stroke_A_meta-analysis_of_case-control_cohort_and_intervention_studies). The Three-City Study also specifically examined olive oil consumption, plasma oleic acid, and stroke incidence, adding cohort-level support (referenced via https://www.nutritruth.org/single-post/the-science-behind-olive-oil-s-top-10-health-benefits).

**Important caveat:** Not all evidence agrees. Healthline notes that a 2020 meta-analysis found no significant link between olive oil intake and stroke risk (https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/11-proven-benefits-of-olive-oil), highlighting inconsistency across studies. Additionally, some analyses caution that olive oil's apparent benefit may partly reflect broader Mediterranean diet patterns (fruits, vegetables, whole grains) rather than olive oil alone, since baseline olive oil intake was very low in some cohorts (https://www.aol.com/articles/happens-stroke-risk-mediterranean-diet-234205542.html).

**Conclusion:** The evidence, especially from the PREDIMED RCT, reasonably supports that olive oil consumption—particularly as part of a Mediterranean dietary pattern—reduces stroke risk. However, conflicting meta-analyses suggest the effect size and independence from overall diet quality remain somewhat uncertain, so the claim is credible but not unequivocally settled.
